mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 5.5% and remains elevated for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, or IC drops below 0.05 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A 6-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals deteriorating demand, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >50% of triggered episodes, or IC < 0.04 over any 4-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% signals improved supply capacity and cost pressures, which raise discount rates and produce positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >55% of triggered instances, or IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals a disinflationary tightening, which lowers long-term yields and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in >50% of triggered episodes, or IC < 0.05 over any 4-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month acceleration in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 0.3% signals labor market strength, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >60% of triggered instances, or IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,000 units signals weakening residential investment, which reduces GDP growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls below 1,000 units for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >55% of triggered instances, or IC < 0.04 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A 6-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals deteriorating demand, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >50% of triggered episodes, or IC < 0.04 over any 4-year window.
